rule: GOAL: Fill the middle slots with colors matching the top row's sequence. CONTROLS: Click a bottom color to select it, then click a middle slot to place it. RULE: The top row dictates the required order for the middle slots. TRAP: Assuming a single click places the color; selection and placement are two separate steps.

GOAL: Turn all switches on so the arch reaches the cup. CONTROLS: Click the bar or stem to toggle that switch’s state. RULE: A switch counts as on only when both its bar and stem are dark. TRAP: Assuming one dark part activates the switch; both must be filled to count as a move.

GOAL: Guide the sliding block to the exit corner without hitting walls. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push the block two spaces in that direction. RULE: The block jumps over one cell, landing on the next valid spot. TRAP: Assuming you can stop on every cell wastes moves; plan for double-length hops.

GOAL: Route the paint into the cup using the blue platform. CONTROLS: Arrows move the platform; Space drops the paint. RULE: Paint flows along the platform to its edge before dripping. TRAP: Thinking the platform pushes the paint; it only guides the flow.

GOAL: Slide the gray shape so its yellow handle aligns perfectly with the yellow gap in the black barrier. CONTROLS: Clicking the gray body shifts the top section right and the bottom section left, creating a shearing effect. RULE: The handle and gap are fixed to opposite ends of the shape, requiring precise horizontal alignment to bridge the barrier. TRAP: Assuming the gray mass moves as a single rigid block; it actually deforms, with top and bottom edges moving in opposite directions.

GOAL: Move the piece along the diagonal line to reach the central gray core. CONTROLS: Click a dot within three steps to move the piece that exact distance. RULE: All valid dots and the core share the same diagonal sum, allowing precise pathing. TRAP: Assuming you must always move three steps wastes time; shorter moves are allowed and often necessary for the final approach.

GOAL: Align the bottom pink row with the top blue row by cycling each glyph to match its column. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor; Up and Down cycled the current glyph forward or backward through the sequence. RULE: Each press shifts the glyph one step; choosing the shorter direction between Up and Down minimizes total actions. TRAP: Assuming only Down works forces extra presses; checking if Up reverses the cycle saves significant time on distant targets.

GOAL: Slide the piston right until its head aligns with the gap. CONTROLS: The lower wall buttons shift boundaries in opposite directions. RULE: Moving the upper wall's lower button creates slack in the middle zone. TRAP: Forgetting to expand the middle space first prevents the piston from reaching the target.

GOAL: Move three boxes into the container slots to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; Space grabs or drops the held box. RULE: You can only carry one box at a time, so plan paths to avoid blocking yourself. TRAP: Assuming you can push boxes freely; you must grab, walk, and drop to position them correctly.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens so the validation band moves past every column. CONTROLS: Click two tokens to swap them; press Space to check the arrangement. RULE: The band highlights the first column with a wrong token, confirming all left slots are correct. TRAP: Assuming the band indicates the last error rather than the first, causing you to fix columns out of order.

GOAL: Lower the first gauge to 42, the fourth to 40, and the fifth to 48 while keeping all gauges between 6 and 58. CONTROLS: Clicking left or right on a column adjusts adjacent gauges by two points, shifting values between them. RULE: No gauge may exceed 58 or drop below 6 at any point during the solution sequence. TRAP: Assuming you could lower the second gauge first fails because the third gauge immediately hits the maximum limit.

GOAL: Arrange the colored blocks so the red and green boxes match the hidden target sequence. CONTROLS: Click two blocks to swap them; press Space to test the current arrangement. RULE: The moving band indicates the first incorrect column, allowing you to isolate and fix errors from left to right. TRAP: Assuming all red blocks fill before green ones; the actual path flows through the pipe, altering the expected order.

GOAL: Rotate pink tiles to match the example pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the selected tile; clicking selects a tile. RULE: Pressing Down cycles through seven distinct classes before repeating, allowing precise class targeting. TRAP: Believing only the final class matters, ignoring that specific rotational poses within a class also require exact matching.

GOAL: Merge two yellow pieces and place the result inside the disc. CONTROLS: Click near a piece to hop it closer; click between two touching same-color pieces to merge them. RULE: Merging takes priority over moving if both pieces are within reach of the click. TRAP: Thinking a click always moves the nearest piece; it actually merges them if both are close enough.

GOAL: Place letters into red, green, and blue boxes to form a single valid word. CONTROLS: Click a palette letter, then click a box slot to place it. Press space to submit your answer. RULE: The green and blue boxes act as entire blocks inserted into specific gaps within the red box sequence. TRAP: Assuming pipes dictate a complex weaving pattern. They simply mark where whole blocks drop in, keeping their internal order intact.

GOAL: Arrange tokens to match the hidden sequence across linked boxes. CONTROLS: Click palette tokens to select, click slots to place, click space to submit. RULE: The pre-placed green token fixes the connector’s position, locking the entire sequence layout. TRAP: Assuming any connector position works wastes time; the fixed green token dictates the only valid placement.

GOAL: Insert blue blocks to make the top sequence match a repeating pattern of three. CONTROLS: Click palette items to place them in red or blue slots; press space to submit. RULE: Only adjacent connector slots create a valid repeating sequence where the inserted blue blocks match. TRAP: Assuming connectors can be placed anywhere; they must be adjacent to ensure the blue blocks align perfectly.

ESTABLISHED: Extending the wire pushes blocks within its span rightward; gripping and moving up pushes swept blocks vertically. FAILED: Moving up while gripping a block with an extended wire pushes other blocks in the path out of bounds. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning blocks horizontally without considering vertical displacement during wire movement. CONTROLS: Extend to push right; grip and move to drag; retract to release.

ESTABLISHED: The 3x3 grid and box are fixed. The cross pattern consists of the center and four cardinal neighbors. The tip is a 4x4 square with two colored halves. FAILED: Completing the cross with the tip oriented up or down did not trigger a win. Clicking grid cells in isolation without completing the shape had no effect. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing the grid or matching the box pattern visually without specific tip conditions. CONTROLS: Clicking grid cells toggles their lit state. Arrow keys rotate the tip's orientation.

GOAL: Reorder the number strip to match the target pattern within five moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift numbers up or down along a hidden cyclic path. RULE: Each cell follows a unique seven-step loop; moving one way advances, the other retreats. TRAP: Assuming numbers increase linearly wastes moves; they actually wrap around in a specific, non-obvious order.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while evading a chasing guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; the guard moves automatically after each turn. RULE: The guard only chases when within range, otherwise it patrols a fixed path. TRAP: Assuming the guard always charges directly at you, ignoring its patrol cycle and range limits.

GOAL: Match each cell's symbol to its target by cycling through classes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; DOWN advances the current cell's class; UP rewinds it. RULE: Classes form a fixed loop; finding the shortest path between current and target classes minimizes presses. TRAP: Assuming you must only press DOWN; ignoring UP doubles the steps needed when the target is behind you in the cycle.

GOAL: Place three colored tokens into three separate boxes to match specific column patterns. CONTROLS: Click source tokens, then click destination slots to place them; spacebar confirms the solution. RULE: Each box requires a unique sequence of colors, determined by the connectors leading to it. TRAP: Assuming boxes could overlap or share slots; they are distinct zones requiring precise, non-overlapping placement.

GOAL: Reach the exit by navigating around stationary guards without entering their facing lines. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step at a time. RULE: Entering a guard's cell from the side or back destroyed it safely. TRAP: Believing front-entry was survivable; touching a guard's facing direction caused immediate failure.

GOAL: Position three platforms over matching cups to fill them completely. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active blue platform; mouse clicks swap which platform is active; space submits the level. RULE: Only one platform moves at a time; clicking a red platform makes it blue and movable, while the previous blue becomes fixed. TRAP: Believing platforms must physically swap places. They do not; only their active status changes, allowing precise independent positioning.

GOAL: Align two crosses to cover specific colored dots on the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross; Spacebar switches control to the next cross. RULE: Each cross must extend its arms to touch all assigned dots simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming moves are fixed-length; observe actual pixel shifts to avoid overshooting targets.

GOAL: Rotate the yellow block to the top-left bracket. CONTROLS: The red arrow rotates the ring counterclockwise; the green arrow rotates it clockwise. RULE: Counterclockwise rotation moves the top row leftward toward the target bracket. TRAP: Thinking the bracket was a movable cursor; it is a fixed destination, and clicking blocks does nothing.

GOAL: Align both sliding bars so their handles land exactly on the fixed plus markers. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the green horizontal bar and yellow vertical bar independently to extend their lengths. RULE: Victory triggered only when a handle centered perfectly within a plus, not merely when bars touched or overlapped it. TRAP: Assuming bar-end contact with the plus was enough; you had to push the handle fully inside the marker.

GOAL: Move the blue block to dock perfectly with the blue shape inside the box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the block one grid step in the chosen direction. RULE: The block cannot overlap the blue shape, treating it as a solid obstacle like a wall. TRAP: Assuming the box was an empty socket; it actually contains a blocker that prevents direct entry.

GOAL: Land the midpoint marker on the target ring. CONTROLS: Clicking empty space moves your cursor there; clicking a partner swaps positions. RULE: The midpoint always sits exactly between your cursor and the partner. TRAP: Thinking you can force the midpoint onto the ring while the partner stays put; you must swap them first.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single remaining peg by jumping over others. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click the landing spot to jump over the middle piece. RULE: Every jump removes the piece you jump over, so plan paths that eliminate all but one. TRAP: Believing you can jump diagonally or in directions other than orthogonal lines wastes moves and blocks progress.

GOAL: Make the highlighted grid match its small preview image. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle their color. RULE: Gray in the preview means blue; white means red. TRAP: Assuming the preview shows a neighbor’s pattern; it is a self-contained target for the current grid.

GOAL: Position three distinct shapes to cover specific target dots. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active shape; Space cycled to the next shape. RULE: A shape only clears dots when its geometry precisely aligns with them. TRAP: Assuming shapes were adjacent when overlapping; one shape’s arms extended far, creating false alignment clues.

GOAL: Match the board’s colors to the hidden pattern shown by the two overlapping mini-grids. CONTROLS: Click a square to cycle its color between blue and orange. RULE: A white square in a mini-grid means that board position must be orange; gray means blue. TRAP: Assuming the mini-grids were independent. They overlap, so one square’s color was dictated by both patterns, forcing a strict match.

GOAL: Move two yellow pieces onto two bracket markers. CONTROLS: Clicks rotate sections clockwise; right-clicks or keys rotate counter-clockwise; other keys shift rows or columns. RULE: Rotations are reversible; tracking only the yellow pieces’ positions simplifies solving without tracking the whole board. TRAP: Assuming a single yellow piece satisfies the win condition wastes time when both pieces must reach their respective brackets.

ESTABLISHED: Two blocks start separate. Moving them adjacent triggers no win. Two bars grow equally with each move, acting as a shared step counter. FAILED: Bringing blocks together did not clear the level. Moving blocks back and forth did not reduce the bar. GOAL IS NOT: Simply merging the two blocks into one position. CONTROLS: Direction keys move both blocks simultaneously. The bar increases with every step taken.

GOAL: Move the active X shape to its target slot. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches focus between shapes. RULE: Only the shape with the white center dot responds to arrow keys. TRAP: Pressing arrows without ensuring the X was active caused wasted moves on the wrong shape.

GOAL: Move the yellow block to its matching slot and the orange block to its own. CONTROLS: Click buttons to rotate the rings; shared cells allow blocks to switch tracks. RULE: Each ring rotates independently, carrying blocks along the circular path to transfer them. TRAP: Assuming blocks stay on their starting ring; you must utilize the shared cells to swap tracks.

ESTABLISHED: The two colored blocks move independently on a grid. The decorative frames act as solid obstacles, not targets. FAILED: Placing blocks against or inside the frame boundaries does not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Aligning blocks with the visible frames or overlapping their interiors. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected block; switching controls allows independent positioning of each piece.

GOAL: Place blocks into the frame interiors. CONTROLS: Arrows move blocks; clicks select active block. RULE: Blocks slide three cells at once, stopping before walls. TRAP: Frame borders are not walls; blocks can slide over them into the center.

ESTABLISHED: Moving away from a blocked position leaves a gray statue. Reversing direction triggers this. FAILED: Repeatedly pressing the action button while blocked or stuck does not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the exit or collecting items immediately clears the stage. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block. The action button resets position without leaving a statue.

GOAL: Merge the two blocks into a single cell. CONTROLS: Arrows move the left block normally; the right block moves in the opposite direction. RULE: Moving towards each other from a two-square gap causes them to occupy the same spot. TRAP: Assuming blocks block each other; they actually pass through to overlap.

GOAL: Align matching symbols on the grid by rotating independent row and column rings. CONTROLS: Clicking a line rotates its ten symbols one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Each line is a closed loop where the end wraps to the start, shifting symbols predictably. TRAP: Assuming row and column rings are linked; they are independent, so moving one does not affect the other.

GOAL: Cover two dot clusters with matching shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches between them. RULE: Shapes recolor only when their center touches a matching swatch. TRAP: Assuming moving the shape covers dots; you must move the center to the swatch first to change color.

GOAL: Adjust four parameters to align moving blocks with fixed targets. CONTROLS: Click buttons to increment or decrement specific height and width values. RULE: Target positions are calculated directly from the current parameter values. TRAP: Reading state immediately after a click may capture mid-animation frames, causing false mismatches.

GOAL: Move two flowers to their target rings by dragging chain anchors. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the active anchor; click an anchor to switch which one you are dragging. RULE: The flower always sits at the exact center of the anchors in its chain. TRAP: Assuming anchors stay fixed when you move another part of the same chain.

GOAL: Slide the white plug to connect its prongs with the green socket. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug three tiles in that direction. RULE: Align the prong rows vertically before sliding horizontally to make contact. TRAP: Moving horizontally first causes collisions; always adjust vertical alignment before closing the gap.

GOAL: Guide the gray shape to overlap the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the shape three spaces per press. RULE: A mirror line creates a reflected copy on the opposite side. TRAP: Ignoring the reflection wastes time as only the active shape matters.

GOAL: Flip sixteen cells to match a symmetric orange frame. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell flips its own color and its four neighbors. RULE: Each click toggles a plus-shape, so order does not matter for the final result. TRAP: Assuming edge cells are inert wastes time; they are fully active and essential for the corners.

GOAL: Paint the shape to match the mini-patterns, using red for gray cells and orange for white ones. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle through blue, red, and orange colors. RULE: Gray in a mini-template means red, not the background color. TRAP: Assuming gray means no change leaves red cells unpainted, stalling progress.

GOAL: Align the gray shape with the yellow target by repositioning the mirror line. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected element; clicking the vertical line selects it for movement. RULE: The gray shape is a mirror image of the black shape across the selected line. TRAP: Attempting to move the gray shape directly fails; you must move the mirror line itself to shift the gray position.

GOAL: Guide a flower through valid cells to a target by moving slots. CONTROLS: Click a slot, then click a destination cell to move it. RULE: The flower’s position is always the average of the four slots’ positions. TRAP: Believing any move helps; invalid moves occur if the new average lands on a blocked cell.

GOAL: Place two yellow blocks into the designated bracket cells. CONTROLS: Top arrows rotate only the top row; middle arrows rotate the entire continuous loop of cells. RULE: Middle arrows transfer blocks between the top row and the lower path, merging them into one large cycle. TRAP: Assuming top and bottom sections are independent; they are actually connected through middle-arrow transfers.

ESTABLISHED: The board state persists after the wipe animation, and the red bar is currently horizontal. FAILED: Clicking pieces, the checker, the blue square, the yellow box center, the green box center, the divider, and the gray sockets produced no visible change. GOAL IS NOT: The wipe animation is not a level reset or a game over screen. CONTROLS: Clicking elements triggers a right-to-left black wipe that restores the board without altering piece positions.

GOAL: Guide two shapes into their target zones without touching. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; click to select it. RULE: Move the vertical piece up first, then shift it horizontally to clear the path for the horizontal piece. TRAP: Assuming you can move the horizontal piece left while the vertical piece is still in the upper rows causes a collision.

GOAL: Match the grid colors to the mini patterns by clicking cells. CONTROLS: Click plain cells to flip only that cell. Click crosshatch cells to flip that cell and its orthogonal neighbors. RULE: White mini patterns mean the center cell takes the center color, while gray means the opposite. TRAP: Assuming all buttons act independently; ignoring the crosshatch area effect wastes moves trying to fix neighbors individually.

ESTABLISHED: The canvas is a 10x10 grid. The reference panel shows a split pattern (white top, purple bottom). A roller exists but appears fixed or limited in movement. FAILED: Attempting to paint the entire canvas to match the reference pattern. Clicking the canvas center and roller fill produced no movement. Up/Down keys did not reposition the roller. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the static reference image via standard painting, as the roller cannot reach all required cells to create the split pattern. CONTROLS: Spacebar likely triggers a stamp. Mouse clicks on the canvas or roller currently

GOAL: Align the reflected line and castle pieces to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; clicks select the line or black shapes. RULE: Objects reflect across the center row, so moving down shifts the reflection up. TRAP: Clicking an already-selected object does nothing, wasting an action if you assume it toggles selection.

GOAL: Navigate the green block to the yellow token. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; clicks toggled switches to open paths. RULE: Blocks must fully enter gray zones to activate them. TRAP: The action bar was time-based, not a step limit; rushing caused errors.

GOAL: Move the last flower onto its matching ring to complete the chain. CONTROLS: Click an anchor to swap the cursor into that chain; click a target to move the flower. RULE: A move is only valid if the flower’s path and landing spot do not overlap other objects. TRAP: Believing any empty cell works; overlapping another chain’s shape blocks the move, wasting turns.

ESTABLISHED: The boat floats at the top of a large connected water body. Row -6 is a solid black barrier blocking upward movement. FAILED: Clicking green blocks in rows -5 to -1 or -11 to -7 does not clear the boat’s path. Horizontal sliding is blocked by column 30. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing adjacent green blocks to create a vertical passage at the boat’s current position. CONTROLS: Clicking green blocks clears a vertical column of rows. The boat slides horizontally on water but cannot cross solid black walls.

GOAL: Place three yellow blocks into their matching yellow brackets. CONTROLS: Right-click rotates a cross; Down-click expands a cross; Click swaps blocks between two specific cells. RULE: Each yellow block is trapped in its own cross and must be rotated or expanded to reach its bracket entry point. TRAP: Assuming blocks can move between crosses; they cannot, as the crosses do not overlap, forcing separate alignment for each block.

GOAL: Place the red ring over two red dots and the blue plus over two blue dots to finish the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Space switches between the ring and the plus. RULE: Each shape must land precisely on its matching colored dots without touching any wrong swatches. TRAP: Assuming the white marker stays visible when shapes overlap; it can hide, causing you to move the wrong piece.

GOAL: Mirror the shape by moving the reflection lines to the center before moving the piece. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object. Clicks select the shape or the lines. RULE: The shape only reflects if it crosses the line’s center column. TRAP: Moving the shape before positioning the lines leaves it unreflected.

GOAL: Align the yellow block at the row edge while rotating the cluster to its target slot. CONTROLS: Red and green buttons rotate rows and columns; one pair also shifts the central cluster. RULE: Parking the block in the column ring lets you rotate the cluster without moving the block. TRAP: Assuming row shifts always move the block; they do not affect it while it is parked in the column.

GOAL: Align eight word slots to their target shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor; Down/Up cycles glyph classes. RULE: Match each slot’s shape to its designated target class. TRAP: Assuming a fixed sequence order; the cursor cycles independently of the shape logic.

GOAL: Clear the green block to open a water passage, then align the boat to reach the win symbol. CONTROLS: Click clears blocks; arrow keys move the boat left or right along the water. RULE: The boat body must fully fit within the cleared water columns to rise or move through. TRAP: Assuming the click opens the entire row; it only clears a small patch, requiring precise boat alignment.

GOAL: Move two puzzle pieces to specific target spots on the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the selected piece; mouse clicks select pieces. RULE: Pieces slide freely until hitting walls or other pieces, requiring careful sequencing to avoid blocking paths. TRAP: Assuming pieces can jump over others or move diagonally wastes time; they only slide in straight lines and must be ordered to clear paths.

GOAL: Merge two blocks into one. CONTROLS: Arrows move both blocks; right mirrors left. RULE: Red tiles kill you; one death resets the whole level. TRAP: Assuming safe paths are symmetric; the right block hits reds the left misses.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while avoiding a patrolling orange enemy that bounces between walls. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per turn; the enemy moves simultaneously in its facing direction. RULE: The enemy flips direction upon hitting a wall, creating a predictable oscillation pattern you must time your moves against. TRAP: Assuming the enemy stays still or moves randomly; ignoring its fixed bounce cycle leads to fatal collisions when paths intersect.

GOAL: Move a flower to three specific waypoints using three sliding slots. CONTROLS: Click a slot, then click a destination tile to shift the flower. RULE: The flower's position is the sum of the three slot positions. TRAP: Believing one slot move could reach distant targets; multi-step sequences were required.

GOAL: Move the green piece to collect the red token and trigger the red mechanism. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green piece; clicking the red podium activates the red bar. RULE: The green piece must fully cover the red token to trigger the podium’s function. TRAP: Clicking slightly off-center on the podium fails; aim for the wide base, not the narrow top.

GOAL: Align three platforms into distinct target zones using minimal moves. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected platform; clicks select platforms; space confirms completion. RULE: Platforms lock in place once deselected, preventing further movement. TRAP: Moving the lower platform last blocked the vertical path for the upper one.

GOAL: Slide two blocks into their respective target rooms to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the currently active block; mouse clicks select a different block. RULE: Only the selected block responds to movement; clicking activates a new target. TRAP: Assuming clicks count toward the movement budget; they do not, only arrow presses matter.

GOAL: Guide two blocks to marked zones by shifting reflection lines first. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected lines or pieces; clicks select targets. RULE: Move lines before pieces, as paths depend on final reflection positions. TRAP: Assuming line moves don't alter collision paths, causing blocked routes.

GOAL: Place both frames into outlines and the token into the small square. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green token, pushing any frame it hits. RULE: Push frames only when aligned with their target slots; never push into walls. TRAP: Over-shooting a frame’s row wastes moves; count steps carefully before pushing.

GOAL: Reach the yellow token at the far right edge. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green block; clicking the red bar rotates it. RULE: Rotate the red bar vertically to bridge the gap between purple platforms. TRAP: Believing the red bar was merely an obstacle; it was actually the necessary bridge.

GOAL: Extend the sky and pink bars so their handles rest on the plus marker. CONTROLS: Click plus signs to lengthen the bars toward the target. RULE: Handles must land on the marker’s arms; bodies cover the center. TRAP: Aiming the handle exactly at the center is impossible due to length constraints.

GOAL: Move two distant pieces to meet and merge, then shift the combined piece to the target. CONTROLS: Click a spot to move a piece if it is within reach; click a meeting point to join two nearby pieces. RULE: A piece only moves to spots close enough to its current position; merging requires both pieces to be close to the click. TRAP: Assuming any click moves a piece regardless of distance; clicks too far from a piece do nothing, wasting turns.

GOAL: Navigate a grid past moving guards to reach a safe exit without being caught. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one square per turn. RULE: Guards move predictably every turn; you must time your moves to slip through gaps when they look away. TRAP: Assuming guards stay still; they patrol actively, so pausing or moving randomly often leads to instant capture.

GOAL: Navigate to the exit while avoiding patrols and eliminating red guards. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per turn. RULE: Attacking a red from the side or back destroys it; entering its front kills you. TRAP: Assuming guards pass through each other safely ignores that they block movement and kill on contact.

ESTABLISHED: Two blocks exist. A central wall divides the area. Three target dots are visible. FAILED: Moving blocks to align across the wall gap did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning the blocks opposite each other across the divide. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move blocks. They slide until hitting a wall or another block.

ESTABLISHED: Green overlaps Purple’s prong, creating a gray block; body bounding boxes confirm current positions. FAILED: Repeated path searches and state verifications without executing the move; previous coordinate readings were inconsistent. GOAL IS NOT: Clearing the level immediately or assuming the gray block is a static obstacle rather than a result of overlap. CONTROLS: Clicking selects objects; arrow keys translate; space rotates clockwise; execution requires verifying the mate pair before moving.

GOAL: Align the plus block with the frame’s hole to complete the shape. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green block; clicks confirm placement or trigger interaction. RULE: A push only registers if the moving block has at least fifteen empty cells of travel room. TRAP: Believing partial alignment wins; the block must slide fully into the designated socket distance.

GOAL: Move the boat left to avoid a hazard, then open the wall above to rise to the upper water level. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the boat; clicks removed blocks to create channels for the boat to float through. RULE: The boat rises only when a block directly above it is removed, allowing it to float to the surface. TRAP: Rising immediately from the starting position caused death by hitting a purple obstacle; you must shift left first.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking both parts of a switch turns it fully on; the side panel displays a pattern of dark bars and stems. FAILED: Clicking only the top bar or only the bottom stem to create a half-on state has not been tested or confirmed to work. GOAL IS NOT: Simply turning all switches fully on, as the side panel hints at partial activation patterns. CONTROLS: Clicking the top bar or bottom stem toggles that specific part of the switch independently.

GOAL: Guide the green block through the U-shaped chamber to the frame exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green block; UP activates the piston mechanism. RULE: The piston pushes the green block when the U-stack is fully red. TRAP: Mistaking the piston's push for a teleport; the green moves physically, not instantly.

GOAL: Guide the shrinking tip through the narrow neck to merge with the head. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the tip; clicks complete traces to toggle its size. RULE: The tip must be two units wide to fit through the two-row neck. TRAP: Believing a large tip can pass through the neck wastes actions on failed moves.

GOAL: The level required navigating the maze to collect specific items and deliver a block to a marked box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block one step at a time across the grid. RULE: The puzzle was solved only when the block landed precisely on the target box after completing all necessary steps. TRAP: Believing that a direct path to the box would work cost time, as collecting required items first was essential.

ESTABLISHED: Moving costs energy; the bar depletes on every step. FAILED: Walking directly to the box and grabbing from the side or diagonal never worked. GOAL IS NOT: The box is not in the starting position, and simple side-grabs are invalid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move and face direction; Space grabs the block directly in front of your facing.

GOAL: Match the three-cell shape to clear the grid and shrink the block, then guide it up the shaft. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to draw the pattern; arrow keys move the block along the vertical path. RULE: The block must be small enough to fit the narrow gap before moving upward. TRAP: Assuming arrow direction changes with orientation; UP always moves up, regardless of the block's shape.

ESTABLISHED: Arrows move the orange socket along the wire. Clicking the plug triggers a level reset. The wire ends three cells away from the plug. FAILED: Moving the socket to the wire's end near the plug did not complete the circuit. Clicking the plug never solved the puzzle, only restarting it. GOAL IS NOT: Simply bringing the socket adjacent to the plug. The plug is not a static decoration to be ignored, nor is it directly movable. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected socket. Clicking the plug resets the level. No other inputs have shown effect.

GOAL: Move all three plugs until every prong overlaps another, leaving zero red prongs. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected plug; clicks switch selection; space confirms or resets. RULE: Prongs mate only when their tips land on the exact same coordinate. TRAP: Assuming prongs stick together once touched, causing you to move them as a single unit instead of adjusting positions independently.

GOAL: Rotate the roller to specific angles to paint distinct regions on the canvas. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the roller clockwise or counter-clockwise; Space stamps the current color; Clicks select colors. RULE: Each arrow press rotates the roller by a fixed increment, aligning it with different painting zones. TRAP: Assuming arrow keys move the roller linearly rather than rotating it around the canvas center.

ESTABLISHED: Gate 2 opens, but water does not flow through it. Pockets 1 and 2 share a fixed volume of 110, keeping the head between rows 44 and 62. The gap is at rows 29-30, making alignment in Pocket 1 impossible. FAILED: Pressing W3-left or W1-left with Gate 2 open. Clicking the head or the yellow gap directly. GOAL IS NOT: Aligning the head with the gap inside Pocket 1. CONTROLS: W1 and W3 shift water between adjacent pockets. Clicking gates toggles their state.

GOAL: Paint a split canvas with purple top, white bottom, and an orange southeast corner. CONTROLS: Click swatches to select colors, arrow keys to move the roller between edge slots, and spacebar to stamp the entire half-plane. RULE: Stamps overwrite previous layers, so apply the largest background halves first before adding the smaller corner detail. TRAP: Moving diagonally requires two orthogonal steps; trying to jump directly from North to South wastes turns and breaks the sequence.

ESTABLISHED: Red box slots 1-3 are Red, Yellow, Orange. Blue box contains Blue, Navy, Peach. Jumping from Red slot 4 enters Blue box. FAILED: Linear traversal of Blue slots after jump. Cyclic reading from entry slot. Reverse direction reading. All resulted in position 3 being Orange. GOAL IS NOT: Position 3 being Orange. The target value must differ from the direct sequence's third item. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move selector. Enter jumps between boxes. Space confirms sequence.

GOAL: Guide the robot to the target zone by managing its position relative to the neutral block and the wire. CONTROLS: Use arrows to move the robot, which extends or retracts the attached wire, pushing or pulling objects in its path. RULE: The wire only affects objects within its current span; moving the robot can create space to bypass obstacles. TRAP: Assuming all attached objects move together; they only shift if the wire’s span actively covers them during the move.

GOAL: Move the peg-in-socket to the left of the fixed peg, then jump it over to the empty spot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the socket; clicks select the peg and then the destination cell. RULE: A peg can jump over an adjacent peg into an empty space, landing two cells away. TRAP: Believing the socket must align perfectly with the grid center; slight offsets still register as valid clicks.

GOAL: Guide the block to the cup. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block. RULE: The statue blocks the spout, forcing the pool to shift. TRAP: Assuming the statue moves with the block; it stays stuck, keeping the path open.

GOAL: Navigate the snake to the head by tracing a template to destroy a wall, then moving through the opening. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the snake; clicks traced the template to break the barrier. RULE: The snake must pass through the gap created by the trace, not the original path. TRAP: Assuming the bar only drains on movement; clicks also consume energy, risking death if budget is tight.

GOAL: Paint the canvas to match a specific color pattern using directional stamps. CONTROLS: Move the roller to compass points, select colors, and press space to stamp. RULE: Stamps paint large directional sectors, with later stamps overwriting earlier ones. TRAP: Assuming moves work in any direction; the roller only moves along valid compass paths, not directly between opposite points.

GOAL: Paint four distinct regions and activate a yellow block using a limited number of clicks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the roller, SPACE stamps the current color, and clicking the knob applies the selected color to the block. RULE: The final stamp must not cover the block, so place the yellow knob action after the last edge stamp. TRAP: Assuming you can paint the block before the final edge stamp, which incorrectly overwrites the yellow fill with blue.

GOAL: Steer the growing blob’s tip to the center while managing your shrinking energy bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the tip one step; clicking triggered a pulse to expand it. RULE: You must collect the green node to refill the bar before reaching the target. TRAP: Assuming the starting energy was enough to reach the center directly without refueling.

GOAL: Pack four blocks into the player’s slot in strict left-to-right order. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; the wire drags adjacent blocks. RULE: Blocks must stay within the wire’s span to remain attached during movement. TRAP: Assuming intermediate rows are safe; long wires push stray blocks in other rows, blocking progress.

GOAL: Navigate a piece to a target socket by stacking column commands. CONTROLS: Click grid switches to set move directions, then run to execute the column sequence. RULE: A column with a vertical switch executes a single step up, overriding horizontal bars in the same column. TRAP: Believing all switches in a column act simultaneously wastes time; only the vertical switch triggers a move if present.

GOAL: Move the third block up one space so its prongs align with the other two blocks' prongs. CONTROLS: Click the target block to select it, then press the up arrow key to move it. RULE: Victory occurs only when every prong on every block touches a prong from another block. TRAP: Assuming the existing touch point involved the moving block; it was already paired, leaving the third block isolated.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to flip a hidden legend shape to match the target, then push a block into the box. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; stepping on a plus sign flips the legend color. RULE: The legend must match the target shape and color before the block can be pushed into the goal. TRAP: Assuming vertical paths are open; a gap in the column forces a longer detour around the obstacle.
